summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and a history of MSSA bacteremia presented with a five-day history of dry cough, body aches, dizziness, and chills, raising concern for recurrent bloodstream infection. He was admitted for observation and started on intravenous vancomycin. Blood cultures remained negative over 48 hours, influenza testing was negative, and he remained afebrile. His symptoms improved, and the antibiotic was discontinued. Thrombocytopenia was noted, possibly due to viral bone marrow suppression or dialysis-related heparin exposure; PF4 antibody testing was pending at discharge. He received scheduled hemodialysis during admission and was discharged home with instructions to follow up for repeat blood work and monitor symptoms. The final diagnosis was viral upper respiratory infection.
